items.title: # saves a rule instantly
items.summary: Start a message with # and it's filed into memory — no file editing, no /memory.
items.detail: The lowest-friction way to build a good CLAUDE.md: every time you correct the agent on something it should have known, retype the correction with a # in front. After a week the file writes itself out of your actual frustrations.
items.snippet: # this project uses pnpm, never npm

items.title: ! runs bash without a round trip
items.summary: Prefix with ! to execute a shell command directly and drop its output into context.
items.detail: No model turn, no permission dance — the command runs and the result is in the conversation. Perfect for handing over a test failure, a directory listing or a git log without describing it.

items.title: @ pulls a file or directory into context
items.summary: Type @ and a path to reference it precisely instead of describing it.
items.detail: Tab-completes paths. Works on directories too, giving a listing rather than a dump. Cheaper and more accurate than 'the config file in the utils folder somewhere'.
items.snippet: Why does @src/auth/session.ts drop the refresh token?

items.title: Shift+Tab cycles permission modes
items.summary: One keystroke between normal, auto-accept edits and plan mode.
items.detail: The most-used invisible control in the whole tool. Tap into plan mode before anything architectural; tap into auto-accept when you're grinding through a mechanical change you've already approved the shape of.

items.title: Esc Esc rewrites history
items.summary: Double-tap Escape to jump back and edit an earlier message, forking the run.
items.detail: Better than arguing with a bad turn: go back to the message where the misunderstanding started, fix the wording, and let it replay from there. Single Esc just interrupts the current action — also underused.
items.snippet:
[Esc]      interrupt
[Esc][Esc] go back and edit an earlier message

items.title: Thinking has a dial
items.summary: "think" < "think hard" < "ultrathink" — the words map to real reasoning budget.
items.detail: Spend it where it pays: architecture, concurrency, tricky algorithms, ambiguous bug reports. On mechanical edits it's wasted money and slower output. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS in env sets the ceiling.
items.snippet: ultrathink about how to make this migration reversible

items.title: Paste screenshots straight in
items.summary: Ctrl+V an image into the prompt — a broken UI is faster shown than described.
items.detail: Works for design targets, error dialogs, dashboards and whiteboard photos. Note it's Ctrl+V for the image paste, not the usual terminal Cmd+V on macOS. Dragging the file in works too.
items.snippet: [Ctrl+V]  →  "the spacing here is wrong below the header — fix it"

items.title: Pipe anything into it
items.summary: It's a unix citizen: stdin goes in, structured output comes out.
items.detail: `cat`, `git diff`, `kubectl logs`, `jq` — anything that prints can be a prompt input, and --output-format json makes the result something the next command in the pipe can parse.
items.snippet: kubectl logs deploy/api --since=1h | claude -p "Find the error pattern and name the likely cause"

items.title: CLAUDE.md can import other files
items.summary: @path syntax composes memory instead of copy-pasting one enormous file.
items.detail: Keep a lean root CLAUDE.md that imports conventions, architecture notes and per-package rules. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files are picked up when the agent works in that folder, which keeps monorepo context relevant instead of total.

items.title: Slash commands can run shell first
items.summary: A !`command` line in a command file injects live output into the prompt.
items.detail: This is what makes custom commands feel magic: /standup can run git log itself, /fix-issue can fetch the issue body, /deploy-check can read CI status — all before the model sees a single token.
items.snippet:
---
allowed-tools: Bash(git log:*)
---
Summarise my day: !`git log --since=yesterday --oneline --author=$(git config user.email)`

items.title: Ctrl+B backgrounds a long command
items.summary: Send a dev server or long build to the background and keep working.
items.detail: Long-running processes used to block the session. Background them and the agent keeps going, checking output when it needs to — the natural pattern for 'start the dev server, then fix the page'.
items.snippet: [Ctrl+B]  while a build or server is running

items.title: /vim
items.summary: Modal editing in the prompt box, for the people who will not be talked out of it.
items.detail: Turns on vim keybindings for composing messages — genuinely useful when you're writing a long, carefully-structured prompt rather than a one-liner. /terminal-setup fixes Shift+Enter for newlines while you're in there.

items.title: Subagents protect your context window
items.summary: The real reason to use them isn't specialisation — it's that their token spend isn't yours.
items.detail: A subagent searching forty files burns its own context and hands back a conclusion. Your main conversation stays clean and long-lived. Use them for fan-out searches, reviews and research; keep the decisions in your own window.
items.snippet: Use a subagent to find every call site of this API and report back — don't paste the files into our conversation.

items.title: --dangerously-skip-permissions
items.summary: The flag everyone reaches for and few should. Container it, or don't use it.
items.detail: It disables every approval prompt. Fine inside a throwaway container with no credentials and no network; reckless on your laptop with your SSH keys mounted. The correct fix for prompt fatigue is an allowlist in /permissions, not this.
items.snippet:
# only inside a disposable sandbox
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w img claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
